text:
alex: heads up — alerts for gpupool-us-west1-3: multiple nodes moved to NotReady and pods are stuck Pending/NoSchedule. noticing ~6 nodes affected, cluster-autoscaler already started adding on-demand replicas which is spiking cost

shreya: which alert fired? CA events?

alex: alert came from node-exporter: node_status_not_ready and k8s-pods Pending for gpu workloads. also infra-alert: high-autoscaler-activity. sounds like aftermath of the kernel upgrade window ~03:20 UTC (deploy-bot did a rolling kernel bump).

deploy-bot: kernel-rollout job for gce-gpu-images completed for us-west1 zone at 03:18 UTC. no errors reported from rollout controller.

carl: I ssh'ed into one NotReady node. kubelet logs show device-plugin crash loop: 
```
E0318 03:25:10.123456  1234 device_plugin.go:200] failed to start plugin: failed to load nvidia driver: module not found
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
```
also dmesg contains: 
```
[   22.345678] nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing
[   22.345689] nvidia 0000:01:00.0: DMA: can't borrow IOMMU domain: -16
[   22.345700] nvidia: probe of 0000:01:00.0 failed with error -16
```

maria: the device-plugin pods are failing liveness and the daemonset is constantly restarted. k8s marks node NotReady because kubelet can't mount GPU resources.

shreya: CA reacted and spun up 4 extra preemptible GPU nodes to satisfy pending pods, but they failed the same way and ended up NotReady -> more churn. Cost is visible on dashboard. we should pause autoscaling for gpupool until we stabilize.

alex: agreed — plan: 1) cordon remaining healthy gpupool nodes 2) pause cluster-autoscaler autoscaling for gpupool nodegroup (or set max= current) 3) drain and reprovision one node manually to validate driver fix 4) roll back kernel on affected image families if needed 5) patch device-plugin to tolerate missing module and retry slower so it doesn't crash-loop and cause kubelet pressure

carl: quick mitigation commands I ran: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpupool-us-west1-3
kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
gcloud compute instances reset <instance>
```

maria: also temporarily added annotation to nodegroup to protect from scale-down: 
```
apiVersion: autoscaling.gke.io/v1
kind: NodeGroup
metadata:
  annotations:
    autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled: "true"
```

ops-bot: INC-2345 created for follow-up: investigate kernel module signing, gke image pipeline, and add readiness probe to nvidia device-plugin. Assigned to @carl and @shreya.

shreya: we should avoid full rollback unless necessary. first try: restart nvidia modules + device-plugin on one repro node: 
```
ssh node
sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia
sudo modprobe nvidia
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -n kube-system
```

carl: tried modprobe sequence — on one node module failed to insert due to signature verification. kernel is using secureboot/enforced module sigs. the new image build omitted signing step. rebooting into older kernel (v5.15) allowed module to load.

maria: so either sign modules in our image pipeline or ensure kernel-image and driver versions are matched. I propose: 1) revert node image to previous working image for the pool 2) update image pipeline to run `kmodsign` step and add test that modprobe nvidia succeeds in a VM 3) add a pre-rollout probe that ensures device-plugin can register before marking node Ready

alex: for immediate cost containment, I set CA max for gpupool to current and scaled down the extra preemptibles we accidentally created. will leave nodegroup cordoned until we confirm driver fix.

shreya: low-risk upgrade path: add a slower backoff to device-plugin liveness probe and change restartPolicy to OnFailure? also add hostPID or hostNetwork? Not ideal. Better: make the plugin a DaemonSet with init container that checks for /dev/nvidia0 before marking ready.

carl: agreed on init container. shared small patch snippet I want to try: 
```
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-nvidia
  image: busybox
  command: ["sh","-c","for i in $(seq 1 30); do [ -e /dev/nvidia0 ] && exit 0 || sleep 2; done; exit 1"]
```
this prevents the main container from starting until node has modules loaded.

maria: pragmatic next steps timeline: 
- 03:40 UTC: cordon remaining nodes and pause autoscaler (done)
- 03:50 UTC: repro on one node, confirm modprobe or reboot fixes (in progress)
- 04:30 UTC: if repro succeeds, roll out image rollback for gpupool and uncordon nodes
- 05:00 UTC: follow-up PR to image pipeline (kmod signing) + device-plugin initContainer

alex: update for the channel: repro succeeded on a test node by booting an old kernel and then applying the signed driver. device-plugin stayed healthy. rolling rollback of the node image group started (will take ~45m).

carl: CA unpaused only for control plane pools, gpupool remains frozen. ops-bot logging cost alert suppression until we finish.

maria: after rollback and testing, we should also add a cluster-autoscaler scale-up cooldown for gpu nodegroups (e.g., 10m) and an explicit budget cap to avoid runaway on-demand spend when device issues happen again.

shreya: filing doc with actionable runbook: how to triage nvidia module vs device-plugin vs kubelet NotReady, and when to pause autoscaling / revert images. will link to INC-2345.

alex: thanks everyone — keeping cordon in place until all nodes validated. will post final update when uncordoned. :thumbsup:
